question: Which physical-use and chronological comparisons can the preserved corpus support?
outcome: Informative depth appears in 2,810/5,680 rows; an earlier rule counted 2,870 placeholder strings as present. Metadata repeats across object faces. Three Harappa physical-use groups contain 69 source objects, 60 joined objects and only two objects in the main >=3-sign population. All 66 faces of 22 copied tablets are complete two-sign observations.
challenge: Placeholders, duplicated object metadata, site-dependent chronological labels and ambiguous identifier punctuation change apparent coverage.
remedy: Row/family counts, explicit placeholder and interval categories, full source introduction acquisition, separately frozen cohort/identifier refinements and source-coordinate checks.
retry_when: Object plates/basic-data tables resolve identifiers or new independently dated/attached-object observations support a defined comparison.
